title: Minkowski LLL relation search
objective: Implement archimedean Minkowski-weighted LLL relation search, capability-aware automorphism orbit planning, differential tests, and a representative benchmark without changing exact relation replay

handoff.summary: Default bounded relation search now reduces the true canonical Minkowski embedding: real coordinates have weight one, complex representatives contribute sqrt(2)-weighted real and imaginary coordinates, and 128-bit midpoint values are converted directly to fixed-point integers without binary64. Exact LLL tracks a unimodular row transform and applies it to the exact ideal basis; plan verification checks determinant, embedded-row reconstruction, exact-row reconstruction, and ideal membership. Random candidate extension skips degenerate zero settings, polls the runtime interrupt hook, and has a draw budget independent of accepted candidates. The completed ideal-class inverse map no longer silently stops at 128 candidates: its default exhausts deterministic exact coefficient shells, while explicit bounds and cancellation return immutable resume cursors with canonical SHA-256, exact schema/type validation, algebraic cursor consistency, verifier-owned size/work limits, and exact prefix replay that rejects even a correctly rehashed cursor skipping a successful candidate. Successful results replay exact principal ideal equality. Relation admission, serialization, and replay schemas are unchanged. Sage's documented nonreal cubic embedding is a differential oracle, precision-stability and exact transform replay cover a real quadratic, and a representative benchmark covers degrees two and three. Because the repository exposes only abstract Galois-group permutations, a public capability plan explicitly selects independent Minkowski search instead of inventing unverifiable automorphism-derived relations.
risks: Archimedean values are high-precision FLINT midpoints rather than certified Arb enclosures; they select only a unimodular basis transform, while all admitted relations remain exact and replayable.
Automorphism-orbit derivation remains unavailable until exact field self-maps, ideal images, and authenticated factor-base permutations share a public protocol.

Unbounded ideal reduction is total only under the completed class-group invariant that the supplied factor base generates every ideal class; standalone callers with an arbitrary incomplete factor base should use an explicit resource bound.
The focused Linux x64 lane does not exercise required Windows or arm64 hosts; the implementation is ordinary Python and uses no new native dependency.
next_steps: Integrate the module, focused test/fixture, and benchmark without changing class_unit_groups.py.
Run central broad gates and platform CI after merge.
If exact automorphism maps are later added, extend the capability planner and derive each orbit record through the existing exact collector replay path.
